title: Speculative fanout decider: kernel-fingerprint priming, confidence gating, and multi-tier fallback
creator: Luca Moreno
description:
Goal: ship a low-risk speculative fanout decider that primess kernel-level fingerprints during prefill, scores tentative decode outputs for early acceptance, and falls back to multi-tier strategies with measurable SLOs. Motivation: current optimistic decode routing reduces latency for a subset of workloads but has two pain points: (1) misrouted speculative work wastes GPU cycles when acceptance fails late, and (2) kernel heterogeneity (quantization, kernel availability) makes candidate selection brittle. This ticket defines a decider that (a) quickly fingerprints the kernel+quantization compatibility during prefill probe, (b) computes a confidence score for early acceptance using lightweight heuristics (entropy delta, token agreement, softmax peakedness) and RL-calibrated thresholds, and (c) maps confidence buckets to a deterministic fallback plan (single-model retry, multi-model fallback, regional handoff).

Scope and deliverables: 
- Design doc: scoring function, feature set extracted during prefill, acceptance thresholds, and fallback mapping. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/speculative-fanout-decider (draft).
- Implementation: kernel-fingerprint sampler (GPU-side microprobe), confidence estimator integrated into prefill path, deterministic fallback orchestrator that can issue follow-up requests with controlled TTL.
- Telemetry: per-request timeline markers (prefill_probe, fingerprint_done, tentative_accept, fallback_trigger), histogram of time-to-accept and wasted speculative token-time. Dashboard: /dashboards/spec-decider-latency.
- Rollout plan: shadow mode -> gradual canary (5%, 25%, 100%) with automated rollback on increased cost or drop in acceptance precision below 95% for latency-sensitive routes.

Acceptance criteria (SLO-driven):
- Median end-to-end latency for prioritized fast-path routes improves by >=6% at 25th-75th percentiles in canary traffic.
- Speculative wasted-GPU-token-time reduced by >=30% vs baseline on A/B test.
- Fallback success rate >= 99.5% (fallback yields an acceptable response within SLA).
- No increase in 99.9th token-latency across all routes.

Design trade-offs considered: 
- Doing heavier prefill probes (longer kernel tests) improves fingerprint confidence but adds latency; we choose microprobes limited to <2ms per request on average to keep overhead low.
- Confidence estimator complexity: a small XGBoost-like model at edge vs heuristic rules. Chosen: heuristic rulebook initially, with telemetry hooks to train a lightweight parametric model in future cycles.
- Fallback aggressiveness: conservative thresholds reduce tail cost but miss some fast-path opportunities. We will tune thresholds per-route via rollout.

Open questions / risks:
- Kernel fingerprint stability across driver updates; mitigation: tag fingerprints with driver/OS metadata and invalidate-old fingerprints post-upgrade.
- Burst behavior where many concurrent speculations cause degraded probe throughput; mitigation: global probe rate limiter and backpressure to normal routing.

Links to artifacts and PRs: 
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/speculative-fanout-decider
- Telemetry dashboard (draft): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/spec-decider-latency
- Implementation PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4291
- Benchmark runs: gs://redwood-bench/spec-decider/2025-02-28/report.csv

Next steps:
- Implement kernel-fingerprint sampler and expose proto (ENG spike: 3d)
- Wire tentative-accept signal into routing layer and add test harness (integration tests + perf harness)
- Start shadow trial on non-critical routes for two weeks, collect telemetry and tune thresholds

Estimated risk: medium. Implementation is invasive in the request fast-path and requires careful telemetry and rollback controls. This ticket coordinates with infra (to add rate-limit knobs) and telemetry owners to ensure dashboards are available before canary.
